notes: DOCUMENT-LEVEL rule. The threshold is PAGE_WEIGHT_THRESHOLD_BYTES = 1_500_000 bytes (1.5 MB) as defined in sustainability.ts. totalBytes is the sum of resource.size (defaulting to 0 when absent) across all entries in PropertySnapshot.networkResources. The HTML markup alone cannot trigger this rule; the test harness must supply networkResources with size fields. Severity is always 'serious'. The finding selector is ':root'. The finding message includes both the MB value and the estimated CO2e figure (computed from estimateCo2eGrams).

cases.why: networkResources sum to 2,035,000 bytes, which exceeds PAGE_WEIGHT_THRESHOLD_BYTES (1,500,000). The evaluate() function fires wsg-page-weight with severity 'serious'.
networkResources sum to 95,000 bytes, well below 1,500,000. totalBytes <= PAGE_WEIGHT_THRESHOLD_BYTES so no finding is generated.

alsoExpectNote: For fail-1 the harness supplies image/jpeg resources so wsg-image-format also fires (unoptimizedImageCount > 0). The estimateCo2eGrams formula in sustainability.ts (bytes * 0.000000414 kWh/byte * 442 gCO2/kWh) produces 372.4 g CO2e for 2,035,000 bytes, which maps to rating 'F' (threshold >= 1.0 g). Therefore wsg-carbon-rating also fires at severity 'serious'. Note: with the code's formula, any networkResources totalling more than ~5,465 bytes on a non-green-hosted page already triggers rating F — this is a known scale discrepancy in the implementation that fixture authors must account for when designing pass cases for wsg-carbon-rating.
